sentences.text: Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal Order on Board (06.05.2024)

1 . This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 by the appellant
against the award dated 15.07.2015 passed by learned Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Kondagaon (C.G.) in Claim Case No.151/2012, awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/- in favour of
the appellant/claimant.

Neutral Citation 2024:Cghc:16468
2.

The averment in the claim petition, in brief, is that on 26.07.2010 at about 4 p.m., when the appellant after parking his motorcycle at forest Naka was calling his friend Vijay Kumar Sahu from the shop, at that time, the offending vehicle i.e. Indica car bearing registration No. C.G.-07-M- 9252,
which was being driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligence manner, dashed his Ashok Chandel vs Yakesh Kumar Mithlesh on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79240027/
1 motorcycle, as a result of which, he suffered injuries on his hands, legs, head, chest and his left thigh got fractured.

sentences.text: The claimant preferred an application before the Claims Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs.16,60,000/-.
Learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents available on record, awarded compensation of Rs.25,000/- in favour of the claimant against which the present appeal has been preferred.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has not considered the medical bills produced by the appellant.

He submits that the Tribunal has not considering the evidence in respect of disability which the appellant has suffered on account of the accident and has awarded only Rs.25,000/- as compensation in favour of the appellant.
It is further submitted that the Tribunal has not discussed Issue No.4 in detail while passing the award.
Therefore, the matter may be remanded back to the claims Tribunal for passing the award afresh.
4. Learned counsel for respondent No. 3 submits that the decision passed by the Tribunal is just and proper, hence, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

5. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the documents on record.
6.
In a claim case, learned Tribunal ought to have seen every Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16468 aspect of the case and computed compensation.

The Tribunal should give a conclusion on all the issues of the case, however, in the present case, the Tribunal has not passed a detailed order regarding Issue No.4 based on the evidence brought on record and holding the negligence on the part of the appellant has awarded Rs.25,000/- in his favour.
If rash and negligent driving is not found on the part of the appellant, what would be the award?

This calculation has not been made in the figures based on the evidence presented by the claimant, therefore, in the larger interest of justice, this Court finds this matter fit to remand back to the Tribunal for deciding the claim afresh considering all aspects of the case and material available on record.
7. Accordingly, the award in question is set aside.
The matter is remanded back to the Tribunal to pass a afresh award after considering all the evidence available on record and re- hearing the parties appeared before this Court.
The Tribunal is directed to pass the award afresh within a period of 03 months from the date of receipt of the records.

8. Both the parties are directed to remain present before the Tribunal on 28.06.2024 at 11:00 a.m.
sharply.
9. Accordingly, the appeal stands disposed of.
10. The Registry is directed to send the records of the Tribunal along with a copy of this order forthwith.
